correctness.rationale: Invariance against arbitrary one-coordinate antiderivatives yields \(\mathbb E[yz\mid x]=\mu x\), \(\mathbb E[x(z-a)\mid y]=\mu y\), and \(\mathbb E[xy\mid z]=1\). The three residuals are exactly \(\dot x\), \(\dot y\), and \(-\dot z\), so conditional orthogonality gives the variance defects and the full orthogonality of \(xy-1\) to functions of \(z\). If the vertical defect vanishes, then \(z\) and \(xy\) are constant on support trajectories; Poincare recurrence reduces the dynamics to the scalar autonomous equation \(\dot x=-\mu x+c/x\), whose non-equilibrium trajectories are monotone and nonrecurrent. Thus the measure is supported on the two real equilibria, and the converse is immediate. The packaged checker independently verifies the pointwise residuals, regression algebra, and equilibrium relations.

value.rationale: The Rikitake dynamo was introduced specifically to model irregular polarity reversals, and the sign of \(\dot z=1-xy\) is the instantaneous direction of the vertical variable that participates in that reversal dynamics. The accepted theorem upgrades known global product balances to a full height-resolved law: every compact invariant component has the same unit conditional product on each height fiber. Its exact defect \(\operatorname{Var}(xy)=\mathbb E[\dot z^2]\) converts vertical activity into a directly measurable stationary statistic, while the equilibrium rigidity and both-side threshold law show that every non-equilibrium periodic or compact stationary state must genuinely alternate between \(\dot z>0\) and \(\dot z<0\). The exact decorrelation \(\operatorname{Corr}(z,xy)=0\) for every non-equilibrium compact stationary state is a structural constraint useful for validating numerical invariant-state computations.
